title: Marked cone adjunction and substitution before deriving straightening
statement:
Use the small simplicial categories and coherent realization $\mathfrak C$ of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], marked simplicial sets of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model], and the marked cone diagrams $L_u$ of [lem-coef-marked-cone-generator-calculations]. For any small simplicial set $S$, small simplicial category $I$, and simplicial functor $u:\mathfrak C[S]\to I^{\mathrm{op}}$, the functor $L_u$ preserves small colimits and has a right adjoint $U_u$ on marked enriched $I$-diagrams. Its $n$-simplices over $\sigma:\Delta^n\to S$ are marked enriched natural maps $L_u((\Delta^n)^\flat_\sigma)\to F$, with simplex operators by restriction; an edge is marked exactly when its map extends across $L_u((\Delta^1)^\flat_\sigma)\to L_u((\Delta^1)^\sharp_\sigma)$.

Write $L_S=L_{\mathrm{id}_{\mathfrak C[S]}}$, $U_S$ for its right adjoint, and $T=L_{\Delta^0}$ with right adjoint $U_0$. For $a:A\to B$, let $a_!$ compose the base map with $a$. There are canonical natural isomorphisms
$$L_Ba_!\cong(\mathfrak C[a]^{\mathrm{op}})_!L_A.$$
More generally, for $v:I\to J$, $L_{v^{\mathrm{op}}u}\cong v_!L_u$ and $U_{v^{\mathrm{op}}u}\cong U_uv^*$, where $v^*$ is restriction and $v_!$ is enriched left Kan extension. For a marked $I$-diagram $G$ its value is the marked coend
$$(v_!G)(j)=\int^{i\in I}J(v(i),j)^\sharp\times G(i).$$
Here the coend identifies the action on the mapping factor with the action on $G$, and markings are induced from the displayed marked products. All these isomorphisms commute with identities, composite substitutions, and maps of the input object.

For every vertex $s$ there is a natural marked isomorphism $(U_SF)_s\cong U_0(F(s))$. If $X\to U_SF$ is adjoint to $h:L_SX\to F$, its marked fiber map at $s$ is adjoint under $T\dashv U_0$ to the composite $T(X_s)\to L_SX(s)\xrightarrow{h_s}F(s)$, where the first map is induced by the fiber inclusion and the identity of $s$. For the initial-face inclusion $a:\Delta^{n-1}\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, $n\geq1$, the extension of any marked $\mathfrak C[\Delta^{n-1}]^{\mathrm{op}}$-diagram $G$ has value canonically $G(i)$ at $i<n$ and the empty marked simplicial set at $n$. No model structure over a base, local Kan hypothesis, or straightening equivalence is assumed.

source.place: HTT Definition 3.2.1.2, Proposition 3.2.1.4, Corollary 3.2.1.5, and the vertex adjunction before Lemma 3.2.3.3; marked generators are those in the cone-generator node. No Stacks tag states this simplicial result; HTT is requested in report.md.

proof.text: First construct the asserted marked Kan extension for any marked enriched diagram $G:I\to\mathrm{sSet}^+$. Form the degreewise coequalizer $P(j)=\int^i J(v(i),j)^\sharp\times G(i)$, with relation $[g\circ v(f),z]=[g,G(f)z]$, using the coend definition and the marked product convention. Colimit markings are the images of marked edges of the summands. Postcomposition on $g$ defines the enriched $J$-action; it preserves markings because the mapping factor is sharp. Given an enriched marked map $b:P\to F$, put $c_i(z)=b_{v(i)}[1_{v(i)},z]$. Conversely, from $c:G\to v^*F$ put $b_j[g,z]=F(g)c_i(z)$. Enriched naturality makes this respect the relation, and the unit and action equations show the two formulas are inverse. Both preserve markings: the first inserts a degenerate identity edge, and the second applies the marked enriched action of $F$. This proves $v_!\dashv v^*$ and the displayed coend formula, without a Dwyer--Kan hypothesis.

source.place: Appendix A.3.3, restriction and enriched left adjoint; direct coequalizer and inverse formulas for the ordinary marked adjunction.

proof.text: Forget markings in Step 1. The underlying coequalizer is the ordinary simplicial coend and its same two inverse formulas give the unmarked Kan adjunction. Apply the canonical isomorphism of [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-target-change] with $D=I$, $D'=J$, $\phi=u$, $\pi=v$. It gives the underlying isomorphism $v_!L_uX\to L_{v^{\mathrm{op}}u}X$ induced by the cone pushout. It also preserves and reflects markings. Indeed, a marked coend representative has the form $[g,h^*\widetilde e]$, with $e$ marked in $X$, or with the second entry degenerate; its image is the translate of $\widetilde e$ by the composite of $v(h)$ and $g$, hence marked. In the degenerate case use the marked enriched action on a degenerate edge. Conversely, each generator $k^*\widetilde e$ in the target is the image of $[k,\widetilde e]$, taking $i=u(x)$ when $e$ starts at $x$. Degenerate target edges are also images of degenerate edges under the underlying isomorphism. Thus this is an isomorphism of marked enriched diagrams, natural in $X$.

source.place: Definition 3.2.1.2, Remark 3.2.1.3 and Proposition 3.2.1.4(3); underlying pushout comparison from the existing unmarked target-change lemma, markings checked on their generators.

proof.text: For a marked enriched $I$-diagram $F$, start with the unmarked $U_u$ of [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-quillen] applied to the underlying diagram. For a flat input all marked cone generators come from degenerate input edges. Their cone edges are degenerate (by the collapse $\Delta^1\to\Delta^0$), and their translates have marked image under every enriched map into $F$, because its action uses sharp mapping sets. Consequently every enriched map $L_u((\Delta^n)^\flat_\sigma)\to F$ is marked. The underlying $U_u$ therefore has exactly the asserted set of $n$-simplices, with the asserted restriction operators. Mark an edge when its associated map preserves the extra markings of $L_u((\Delta^1)^\sharp_\sigma)$, equivalently when it extends along the flat-to-sharp map (which changes only markings). Degenerate edges satisfy this condition by factoring through $L_u((\Delta^0)^\flat)$ via the collapse of the sharp edge. Postcomposition with an enriched marked map of diagrams preserves this condition, so this defines a functor to marked simplicial sets over $S$.

source.place: Corollary 3.2.1.5, explicit construction left to the reader; ordinary simplexwise right adjoint from Section 2.2.1 and marked extension criterion from Definition 3.2.1.2.

proof.text: Under the underlying adjunction of Step 3, $h:L_uX\to F$ corresponds to the map sending a simplex $x:\Delta^n\to X$ to $h\circ L_u(x)$. For a marked edge $e$ of $X$, its image in $U_uF$ is marked precisely when $h\circ L_u(e)$ preserves the sharp-edge cone marking. By the cone-generator description this is precisely that $h$ sends $\widetilde e$ and all its translates to marked edges. Requiring this for every marked $e$ is precisely that $h$ is a marked map. Thus the unmarked bijection restricts to the desired marked adjunction, naturally in $X,F$. It implies preservation of small colimits: maps from $L_u(\operatorname{colim}X_a)$ to $F$ are compatible families of maps from $X_a$ to $U_uF$, hence compatible families of maps from $L_uX_a$ to $F$. Small colimits exist degreewise in marked sets over $S$ and objectwise in marked diagrams, with markings generated by summand markings; the enriched action descends by its compatibility with the colimit maps.

source.place: Definition 3.2.1.2, Proposition 3.2.1.4(1), Corollary 3.2.1.5; restriction of the ordinary adjunction to marking-preserving maps, and the maps-out proof of colimit preservation.

proof.text: For $a:A\to B$, the construction $L_B(a_!X)$ and the construction with $S=A$, $I=\mathfrak C[B]^{\mathrm{op}}$, $u=\mathfrak C[a]$ have literally the same pushout: their attaching map is $\mathfrak C[X]\to\mathfrak C[A]\to\mathfrak C[B]$. Their marked cone generators also agree, since the marked edges of $X$ have not changed. Apply Step 2 with $u=\mathrm{id}_{\mathfrak C[A]}$ and $v=\mathfrak C[a]^{\mathrm{op}}$ to identify this construction with $(\mathfrak C[a]^{\mathrm{op}})_!L_AX$. This gives the claimed base-substitution isomorphism on marked objects and on their maps.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.1.4(2)-(3); equality of the attaching maps followed by the already proved marked target-substitution comparison.

proof.text: Apply the adjunctions of Steps 1 and 4 to the marked isomorphism of Step 2. For every $X$ the natural bijections are $\operatorname{Hom}(X,U_{v^{\mathrm{op}}u}F)=\operatorname{Hom}(L_{v^{\mathrm{op}}u}X,F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(v_!L_uX,F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(X,U_uv^*F)$. Evaluating on flat simplices gives the right-adjoint comparison and evaluating on sharp edges shows that it preserves and reflects markings. Coherence can be checked before adjunction. For a second substitution $w:J\to K$, the composite coend comparison sends $[k,[g,z]]$ to $[k\circ w(g),z]$; its inverse sends $[h,z]$ to $[h,[1,z]]$. The action relations give both inverse identities, and these formulas preserve markings. For an identity substitution the formula is $[g,z]\mapsto G(g)z$. Both successive cone-pushout comparisons send an original cone generator to the same generator and old morphisms by the same composite functor; their equality follows from the pushout universal property. All formulas commute with maps of $X$. Their adjoints consequently have the same identity, composition, and naturality compatibilities.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.1.4(2)-(3); explicit coend associator, unit, and uniqueness on cone-pushout factors.

proof.text: Fix a vertex $s$ and put $I=\mathfrak C[S]^{\mathrm{op}}$. Let $i_!K$ be the marked set $K$ over the constant vertex $s$, and let $j:*\to I$ select $s$. Steps 2 and 5 give $L_Si_!K\cong j_!TK$, with $T$ the terminal-index cone functor of the generator node. Step 1 gives $(j_!H)(t)=I(s,t)^\sharp\times H$. A marked enriched map $j_!H\to F$ is determined by $q:H\to F(s)$: its components are $(g,z)\mapsto F(g)q(z)$, with inverse evaluation on $1_s$. Hence the adjunction of Step 4 identifies maps $K\to(U_SF)_s$ with maps $TK\to F(s)$, and then with maps $K\to U_0F(s)$. Here maps $i_!K\to U_SF$ are exactly maps to the marked fiber, by the definition of pullback markings. On flat simplices these mutually inverse formulas give a simplicial isomorphism, and on sharp edges they identify the markings. This proves the claimed natural marked fiber isomorphism for every $F$, even when $s$ has nontrivial endomorphisms in $I$.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 3.2.3.2, printed pp.188-189, the adjunction identifications before using any fibrancy or equivalence argument.

proof.text: Let $h:L_SX\to F$ have adjoint $f:X\to U_SF$. Apply the correspondence of Step 7 to the restriction $X_s\to(U_SF)_s$. Naturality of the adjunction says its adjoint is $j_!T(X_s)\cong L_S(i_!X_s)\to L_SX\xrightarrow h F$. Evaluation at $1_s$ in the explicit inverse formula of Step 7 makes this exactly $T(X_s)\to L_SX(s)\xrightarrow{h_s}F(s)$. The first arrow uses the fiber inclusion and the identity of $s$; it preserves markings by functoriality of the cone generator construction. Thus this is an equality of the specified adjoint maps, including their marking condition, and is natural in both $X$ and $F$.

source.place: Notation before Lemma 3.2.3.3, printed p.189, and the adjunction identification in the proof of Lemma 3.2.3.2.

proof.text: For $a:\Delta^{n-1}\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ omitting the last vertex, let $I=\mathfrak C[\Delta^{n-1}]^{\mathrm{op}}$, $J=\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]^{\mathrm{op}}$, and $v=\mathfrak C[a]^{\mathrm{op}}$. The subset-poset formula for coherent simplices identifies $I$ with the full simplicial subcategory of $J$ on $0,\ldots,n-1$. For $i<n$, Step 1's coend is $\int^k I(k,i)^\sharp\times G(k)$. Its map to $G(i)$ is $[g,z]\mapsto G(g)z$, with inverse $z\mapsto[1_i,z]$. The action relation gives both inverse identities, and the marked action and degenerate identity show they are marked maps. For $i=n$, every mapping set $J(v(k),n)=\mathfrak C[\Delta^n](n,k)$ is empty since $k<n$; every coend summand is therefore empty. This proves the stated values, naturally in $G$. The argument includes $n=1$ and needs no local Kan or model-structure hypothesis.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.1.4(3), applied to the initial-face inclusion; direct subset-poset and coend calculation of its values.
